source.title: Superposition Is Not Necessary: A Mechanistic Interpretability Analysis of Transformer Representations for Time Series Forecasting

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports SAE analyses of PatchTST time-series representations, but does not test whether neuron poles have one or two identifiable jobs, audit explanation accuracy on held-out activations, or test the other listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern superposition signatures in PatchTST, not neuron-pole job counts or the explanation-quality measures in V1–V7. The paper cites prior SAE work as background; those cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on PatchTST post-GELU FFN activations and tests superposition signatures (dictionary scaling, dead latents, latent amplification). It never audits individual neurons' jobs, explains neurons, scores explanations, or builds neuron-based attribution graphs. Its 'no strong superposition' conclusion is thematically adjacent to the essay but measures a different construct (SAE-latent functional relevance), so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors conclude that PatchTST's post-GELU FFN activations show no evidence of strong superposition, so superposition is not necessary for competitive forecasting on standard benchmarks, helping explain linear models' competitiveness.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SAE dictionary scaling and latent interventions on a time-series forecasting transformer; it does not use the neuron-pole audit or explanation-testing procedure described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary across datasets and horizons; the paper reports dead-latent rates exceeding 60% on Traffic and below 7% on most benchmarks.

fits_no_version.finding: In single-layer PatchTST FFN activations, expanding SAE dictionaries from 0.5× to 4.0× changed downstream forecast performance by 0.214% on average.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In small time-series forecasting transformers, overcomplete SAE dictionaries recover no functionally relevant extra structure, consistent with absent strong superposition.

fits_no_version.finding: Amplifying the top-10 4.0× SAE latents by 5× shifted forecasts by ≈0.031 MAE on average (max 0.061).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dominant SAE latents in PatchTST FFN activations individually exert weak causal control over forecasts.

record.problems: The analysis covers one architecture and one hook location (post-GELU FFN activations); the authors note that attention heads and residual-stream representations were not analyzed. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the relevant aggregate results.
record.rows_left_out: Individual dataset-by-horizon dictionary-scale degradation values in Table 1 and dead-latent rates in Table 1 were not extracted; the aggregate dictionary-scaling result is recorded in R1. Table 2 SAE fidelity metrics and Appendix B FFN zero-ablation results do not measure the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole job shares; no neuron-level audit.
Neuron-pole shares in other language models, dense or MoE, at any scale; the study uses a small time-series transformer.
InceptionV1 polysemantic neurons, pose, recursive generalization.
Effect of architecture, regularization or tools on interpretable-neuron share; vision-model estimates.
Neuron-based attribution graphs and replacement-model reconstruction error.
Whether activating-example explanations predict firing elsewhere.
Simulation-based automated scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Neither an original source nor a test. The related-work statement that LLM SAE work 'consistently reveals dense superposition' is cited background, not a result. Any link to the essay's anti-superposition stance would be interpretive only; the study measures SAE latents in a time-series model, not neurons' jobs or explanations. Per-dataset Table 1 values (e.g., Traffic dead latents >60%) are reasonably left out.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole job shares and held-out tests of pole explanations.
Neuron-pole shares across language models, dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, or model scales up to trillions of parameters.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car examples, pose detection, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Interpretability shares for InceptionV1-sized vision models and effects of architecture, regularization, or tools on those shares.
Attribution graphs using a large model's own neurons and their reconstruction error.
Whether explanations matching activating examples predict where neurons fire on other examples.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: PatchTST
rows.size_stated: Single transformer layer; dataset-specific dmodel values range from 16 to 128.
rows.operation_detail: Replaced post-GELU FFN activations during inference with SAE reconstructions at different dictionary sizes.
rows.measure: Average downstream forecasting performance difference between the 0.5× and 4.0× SAE dictionaries.
rows.baseline: Original post-GELU activations; the reported value is the comparison between dictionary sizes.
rows.note: Aggregate across datasets and horizons. The paper describes the difference as negligible; its individual dataset-horizon dictionary degradation values are not extracted here.
rows.check: Link to none is correct. SAE dictionary-scaling effect on forecast MSE in a time-series model, not a neuron-pole job share. Values match text (0.214%).

rows.subject: PatchTST
rows.size_stated: Single transformer layer; dataset-specific dmodel values range from 16 to 128.
rows.operation_detail: Amplified each of the top 10 most highly activated latents in the 4.0× SAE by a factor of 5.0× during inference.

conditions.value: Top 10 by total activation magnitude in the 4.0× dictionary

rows.measure: MAE between original and intervened forecasts (prediction shift).
rows.value: Approximately 0.031 MAE average intervention-induced prediction shift; maximum observed shift 0.061.
rows.note: Aggregate result across benchmarks and horizons; the paper characterizes the shifts as small.
rows.check: Link to none is correct. SAE latent amplification shift (≈0.031 MAE, max 0.061), not a neuron interpretability measure. Values match Section 4.3.
